title: Sherlock Holmes
name: Holmes
same: lean face, hawk nose, slicked-back dark hair, mouse-coloured dressing gown and the black clay pipe
recap: a tall, very thin man of about forty, as Sidney Paget drew him: a high forehead, dark hair slicked straight back, sharp grey eyes, a thin hawk-like nose, a narrow, clean-shaven, keen face; a long mouse-coloured (soft grey-brown) dressing gown with a darker sash and lapels, over a white shirt with a dark cravat; and a straight black clay pipe lying on the felt beside his right hand
keep: The straight black clay pipe lies on the felt beside his right hand (the left of the picture), unlit, unless the pose says otherwise. His mouse-coloured dressing gown is the same in every pose. No hat of any kind.
no: No deerstalker, no cape, no curved calabash pipe, no magnifying glass unless the pose says so, no chair.
intro:
Baker Street's champion and seat 4 (the player's right), seated from the first hand in his own sitting room: drawn facing the viewer's right and MIRRORED by the game to face the table's centre. Built the way Nemo and Javert are (`art-tools/pose_rig.py`), style-locked.

His look, from his character file: Sidney Paget's Holmes, tall and very thin, hawk-nosed, high-foreheaded, in the mouse-coloured dressing gown (The Empty House): he is at home, and the soft grey-brown breaks the table's row of dark coats (Nemo, Javert). No deerstalker (Paget gave him one only in the country) and no curved calabash pipe (a stage invention). His prop is a straight black clay pipe, whose angle at his mouth is the tell surface: it lies by his right hand at rest so his hands stay free for the cards, and he takes it up for two of his tells.

Ruled out (his character file): every modern screen version, 'Elementary, my dear Watson' (Doyle never wrote it), and Moriarty. Layout from Lancelot's character sheet, style from Washington's pose sheet A.

Tags (MOTION-SPEC.md): his three tells, each beside the idle it hides among: putting his fingertips together (strong) beside examining a speck on the tablecloth; drawing on his pipe (bluffing) beside turning his lens over in his fingers; tapping his pipe stem against his teeth (weak) beside glancing at your hands. 'Looks at the mantel as if it had lied to him' is C4.

howto: One fresh ChatGPT chat for all six. The first prompt attaches TWO images, in this order: Lancelot's character sheet (`art-tools/lancelot_parts/sources/lancelot_sheet.png`) for the layout, then Washington's pose sheet A (`art-tools/washington_parts/sources/poses_a.png`) for the style. From the second prompt on, attach Holmes's own character sheet, his pose sheet A once it exists, AND Washington's pose sheet A again, and nothing else.
character:
Character sheet for 2D animation rigging: Sherlock Holmes, of Arthur Conan Doyle's stories (1887-1927), as Sidney Paget drew him for The Strand. Copy ONLY the LAYOUT of the FIRST attached sheet (what goes where): take NOTHING of its character. No plate armour, no gauntlets, no striped surcoat, no long hair. Take the STYLE from the SECOND attached image.

Holmes: a tall, very thin man of about forty; a high forehead, dark hair slicked straight back; sharp grey eyes under level brows; a thin, hawk-like nose; a narrow, clean-shaven, keen face, a little pale; long, thin fingers. He is at home in his own sitting room, so he wears a long mouse-coloured (soft grey-brown) dressing gown with darker lapels and a darker sash, over a white shirt with a dark cravat. His prop: a straight black clay pipe, long and slim, NOT curved. Brilliant, restless, impatient, faintly amused by everyone. NO deerstalker, NO cape, NO curved calabash pipe, NO hat of any kind. Nothing from any film or television version.

Pure white background (#FFFFFF). Every piece separate, with a closed dark outline and a wide gap all round it; nothing touches or overlaps. No text, no labels, no frames, no cast shadows.

The angle: a gentle three-quarter view, turned about 25 degrees from front-on, facing the viewer's right. Both eyes, the whole nose, the mouth and both shoulders clearly visible. NOT profile.

Draw, all facing the viewer's right, at the same size:
- Finished heads, each with the neck and the top of the dressing gown: neutral, keen and watchful; talking, mouth open mid-word; a thin, pleased smile; eyes narrowed, reading someone
- The torso in the dressing gown: no head, cut off straight below the waist, the upper arms down to the elbows; NO forearms, NO hands
- Two forearms in the dressing-gown sleeves with white shirt cuffs, lying on a table, pointing toward its centre, open at the elbow end
- The straight black clay pipe on its own; a round magnifying lens with a short handle on its own
- Four seated reference poses, waist up behind the curved edge of a round green poker table, forearms resting on its edge, hands apart, the clay pipe lying on the felt beside his right hand (the left of the picture): neutral; his fingertips together in front of his chin; drawing on the pipe; tapping the pipe stem against his teeth

A: At rest: both forearms lying along the table's edge, his long hands resting on the felt in front of him, a hand's width apart, relaxed and NOT touching, NOT laced, NOT overlapping; the clay pipe lying on the felt beside his right hand; a keen, watchful look, mouth closed
Peeking at his cards: his right hand cupped over two cards on the felt, thumb lifting the near corner, eyes down
Checking: one long finger of his right hand tapping the felt
Calling: his right hand sliding a short stack of chips forward
Betting: his right hand setting a stack of chips down, precise, well forward
Folding: his right hand laying two cards down face down, bored
B: All in: both hands pushing his whole stack of chips forward, eyes alight
Showing: his right hand turning two cards face up; the card faces are BLANK white, no ranks, no suits
Collecting the pot: both forearms out on the felt, drawing a pile of chips in
His fingertips together: both elbows on the table's edge, his long fingers pressed tip to tip in a steeple in front of his chin, eyes half closed
Examining a speck on the tablecloth: bent close over the felt, his right forefinger pointing at a tiny spot, eyes narrowed
Drawing on his pipe: the straight clay pipe held in his right hand, its stem between his lips, cheeks drawn in, eyes on the table
C: Turning a round magnifying lens over in the fingers of his right hand, in front of his chest, idly
Tapping the stem of the clay pipe against his front teeth, the pipe held in his right hand, eyes narrowed in thought
Glancing at the viewer's hands: eyes cut down and sideways toward the front of the table, head still; arms as at rest
Looking up at a mantelpiece off to the left of the picture, over his shoulder, as if it had lied to him: brows drawn, mouth set; arms as at rest
A sharp, reading look straight at the viewer; arms as at rest
Leaning back in his seat, eyes half closed, bored, his hands loose on the table's edge
D: Talking: his right index finger raised, explaining
Facing a big bet: eyes narrowed, his chin resting on his right hand, elbow on the table
Lost a pot: a thin, irritated smile; arms as at rest
Won a pot: a quick, pleased smile, his right hand drawing a few chips toward him
Down to two players: leaning in on both forearms, eyes bright, eager
Knocked out: rising from his seat, the clay pipe in his right hand, a curt little bow
